g9-geography-ug6-t1.overview: Human-Environment Relationship sits inside Human-Natural Environment Interactions in Ethiopia. Resource use links people and the environment in Unit 6 of Grade 9 Geography in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, the unit shows how humans depend on, modify, and adapt to their surroundings. Then it weighs optimum, over, and under population against the resource use each one allows. Next, it traces the effects of rapid growth before Unit 7: Contemporary Geographic Issues and Public Concerns turns to conservation. Students will also learn how resource use applies to real-life situations such as forests, water, and farmland.
objectives: Describe how people depend on, modify, and adapt to the environment.
Define optimum, over, and under population with examples.
Explain how population size affects the use of resources.
Analyze the effects of rapid growth on forests and soil.
Interpret the graph of under, optimum, and over population.
g9-geography-ug6-t1.simple:
Human-Environment Relationship in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the environment as the physical world of land, water, and air around us.
  • Then the three links, dependence, modification, and adaptation.
  • Also the two big pressures, using natural resources and producing waste.
g9-geography-ug6-t1.detailed:
Human-Environment Relationship — the essentials. First, the environment as the physical world of land, water, and air around us. Then the three links, dependence, modification, and adaptation. Also the two big pressures, using natural resources and producing waste.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Describe how people depend on, modify, and adapt to the environment.
  • Define optimum, over, and under population with examples.
  • Explain how population size affects the use of resources.
  • Analyze the effects of rapid growth on forests and soil.
  • Interpret the graph of under, optimum, and over population.
